title: hello-graph — three nodes, two edges, one human gate (target: graph)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: A 3-node graph — plan → execute → summarise — with explicit edges and state persisted per execution.

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the boot beats.

groups.title: Beat 1 · The spec: three nodes, two edges

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape, pick the entry
beats.cue: “Four lines: the name, the graph spine, the model — and which node the run starts at.”

beats.label: Node 1 · plan
beats.cue: “Read the user's input from the Upstream state and produce a 3-bullet plan.” No preamble.

beats.label: Node 2 · execute
beats.cue: “Read the plan from the Upstream state's plan field and execute it.” Grounded, 4–6 sentences.

beats.label: Put a human in the loop
beats.cue: One block buys an approval gate: the run stops at execute and waits for a person before summarise. The comment says what the gate really does — the checkpoint holds the state from *before* the node, so approving replays it.

beats.label: Node 3 · summarise
beats.cue: “A 2-sentence executive summary. Do not include lists or bullets — prose only.”

beats.label: Wire the DAG
beats.cue: Nodes are inert until you connect them: plan → execute → summarise.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Graph well-formedness passes the compile path skips, plus a scope audit — nothing emitted.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “Nodes, edges and the hitl prompt, lowered to JSON — this is what the compiler actually sees.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target graph (3 nodes, 2 edges, hitlPrompt on execute); the edges carry from/to only — no schema, so they are untyped

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN, with no key in the room.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the credentials gate

beats.label: Open the emitted graph
beats.cue: “addNode, addEdge, setEntry over a checkpoint store — and look inside execute: requestApproval sits after the model turn. The gate is after the work.”

beats.label: Try to ship it to the edge
beats.cue: “Refused: the human gate needs a host. The compiler won't quietly drop it to fit the edge.”

verify.note: deliberate rejection — `cf-worker-graph does not support HITL in M2 (node "execute" has hitlPrompt)`

beats.label: Ask run to run it
beats.cue: “run is the cli/browser REPL. A graph is compile-only — the CLI names the shapes it takes.”

verify.note: deliberate rejection — `crewhaus run supports target: cli or browser (got "graph")`

beats.label: Boot the graph on a real question
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Input on stdin: plan and execute both run, then it stops at the gate and prints its own resume line.”
beats.command: echo 'Draft a launch announcement for the CrewHaus graph starter.' | bun live/dist/agent.ts

verify.note: target graph has no REPL — the emitted bundle reads its input from stdin. Two model calls: the hitl gate is requestApproval AFTER the execute node's turn, and the checkpoint stores the state at the pause, so execute's own output is not committed

groups.title: One more thing · the pause is a checkpoint

beats.label: Look at the run on disk
beats.cue: [needs-key] Every run is a directory of checkpoints — state you can resume from or branch off.

verify.note: the run dir (grun_…) only exists after the keyed run above; the store is .crewhaus/graphs

beats.label: Approve, and let it finish
beats.cue: [needs-key] Approve the newest run. The checkpoint holds the state at the pause, so execute runs again — this time straight through — and then summarise.

verify.note: resumes from the head checkpoint with decision `approve`; ls -t picks the newest graphRunId. The paused node never committed its output, so execute re-runs (a second execute model call) with ctx.approval pre-set, then summarise
